title: CE characteristics of NPN transistor
aim: To plot the input and output static characteristics of an NPN transistor in Common Emitter configuration.

theory.summary: In Common Emitter (CE) configuration, the emitter terminal is common to both input (base-emitter) and output (collector-emitter) loops. Input characteristics represent IB vs VBE for constant VCE, demonstrating diode-like forward bias. Output characteristics show IC vs VCE for constant IB, defining active, saturation, and cutoff regions.

key_formulas.name: Input Dynamic Resistance
key_formulas.variables: r_in in ohms, IB in microamperes

key_formulas.name: Output Dynamic Resistance
key_formulas.variables: r_out in ohms, IC in milliamperes

procedure: Step 1: Connect the NPN base resistor to the VBB supply and the collector resistor to VCC.
Step 2: Keeping VCE constant at 0V, vary VBE and record base current IB.
Step 3: Repeat input readings for VCE constant at 1V and 5V.
Step 4: Keep base current IB constant at 20μA. Vary VCE from 0V to 10V and record IC.
Step 5: Repeat output readings for IB constant at 40μA and 60μA.

observations.what_to_plot: Input characteristics (VBE vs IB) and Output characteristics (VCE vs IC)

expected_results.description: Output current IC should increase rapidly below VCE = 0.7V (saturation), then saturate to a constant level proportional to IB (active region).

common_errors.symptom: Base current is zero while VBE increases
common_errors.fix: Verify BC547 Pinout: Collector, Base, Emitter from flat face left-to-right. Check base connections.

viva_questions.q: Why is the CE configuration widely used in amplifiers?
viva_questions.a: Because it offers high voltage and current gain, providing the maximum power gain among all configurations.

title: Enhancement-mode nMOSFET characteristics
aim: To plot the drain and transfer characteristics of an n-channel Enhancement MOSFET.

theory.summary: An enhancement MOSFET remains off at VGS = 0V. An n-channel is formed when VGS exceeds the threshold voltage Vth, attracting electrons under the gate oxide. Drain current ID flows when VDS is applied, saturating when VDS > VGS - Vth.

key_formulas.name: Saturation Current
key_formulas.variables: kn = conduction parameter, Vth = threshold voltage

procedure: Step 1: Connect gate to VGG supply and drain to VDD supply through the load resistor.
Step 2: Maintain VDS constant at 5V, vary VGS from 0V to 5V and record ID (transfer curve).
Step 3: Set VGS constant at 3V. Vary VDS from 0V to 10V and record ID (drain curve).
Step 4: Repeat drain curve for VGS = 4V.

observations.what_to_plot: Drain (VDS vs ID) and Transfer (VGS vs ID) curves

expected_results.description: Drain current should remain zero until VGS reaches Vth (~2-4V for IRF540N), then increase quadratically.

common_errors.symptom: Drain current does not flow at high gate voltage
causes: Gate oxide is punctured by ESD
common_errors.fix: Always ground your hands before handling MOSFET pins to avoid ESD damage. Verify IRF540 Pinout: Gate, Drain, Source from front left-to-right.

viva_questions.a: It means the channel is absent at zero gate voltage and must be enhanced or created by applying a gate potential.
